parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A take  B make  C hold  D keep → A
parts.title: Why do we laugh?
paras: Laughter is something most of us (0) take for granted, yet scientists are still trying to understand exactly why we do it. One surprising fact that has [[1]] to light is that we are far more likely to laugh when we are with other people than when we are on our own. In [[2]] words, laughter seems to be less about jokes than about relationships.

Researchers who have [[3]] people in everyday conversations found that most laughter does not follow anything particularly funny. Instead, it [[4]] after ordinary comments such as 'See you later' or 'I know!'. It appears to act as a signal that we are friendly and that we [[5]] with the person we are talking to.

Laughter also has physical [[6]]. It can reduce stress, and some studies suggest it may even [[7]] our ability to cope with pain. So the next time you find yourself laughing at something that isn't really funny, don't worry. You are simply doing what humans have always done to [[8]] along with each other.

q.expl: Идиома come to light — стать известным, обнаружиться. Bring to light требует дополнения (bring sth to light).
Устойчивое in other words — другими словами.
observe sb — наблюдать за кем-то (без предлога). Look, glance, stare требуют at.
occur — происходить, случаться. Take/make/set place без «place» не работают.
agree with sb — соглашаться с кем-то. Accept, admit, allow идут без with.
physical benefits — польза для здоровья. Profits и earnings — про деньги, gains — прирост.
Нужен переходный глагол: improve our ability — улучшить способность. Rise и arise не берут дополнения, grow ability так не говорят.
Фразовый глагол get along with sb — ладить с кем-то.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Life on a houseboat
paras: More and more people in big cities are choosing to live on houseboats. For some, it is simply a way of escaping high rents. (0) Others are attracted by the idea of a simpler life closer to nature.

Living on a boat, however, is not [[9]] everyone. Space is extremely limited, so owners have to think carefully about everything they buy. [[10]] is also hard work: water tanks have to be filled by hand, and in winter it can be difficult to keep warm.

Despite this, most boat owners say they would never go back to living on land. They enjoy waking up to the sound of birds, and many describe a strong sense of community. 'Everyone helps each [[11]],' says Tom, who has lived on a canal boat for six years. 'If your engine breaks down, there's always someone who knows [[12]] to fix it.'

[[13]] you are thinking of trying it, experts recommend renting a boat for a few weeks first. That way, you can find [[14]] whether the lifestyle really suits you before you spend a lot of money. After [[15]], a boat is a big investment, and selling one can take months. It is also worth checking [[16]] there are places to moor nearby, as these are becoming increasingly hard to find.

q.expl: not for everyone — подходит не всем.
Нужно подлежащее: It (или This) is also hard work — это (жизнь на лодке) тоже тяжёлый труд.
each other — друг друга.
know how to do sth — знать, как что-то сделать.
Условие: If you are thinking of trying it — если ты подумываешь попробовать… Подойдёт и When.
find out — выяснить.
After all — в конце концов, ведь.
Косвенный вопрос «есть ли»: checking whether there are places… Подойдёт и if.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: The true cost of fast fashion
paras: Fast fashion – cheap clothes that copy the latest catwalk trends – has become (0) incredibly popular over the past twenty years. Shoppers love the [[17]] and the low prices, but there is a growing [[18]] of the hidden costs.

The fashion industry is [[19]] for a significant share of the world's water pollution, and many garments are worn only a handful of times before they are thrown away. Critics also point to the poor [[20]] in which many factory workers are employed.

Some brands have responded by launching more [[21]] collections made from recycled materials. However, campaigners argue that these are often little more than marketing, and that real change will require a [[22]] reduction in the amount of clothing we buy. It may sound [[23]], but repairing your clothes could be the most [[24]] thing you do for the planet.

q.expl: После the нужно существительное: choice — выбор.
a growing awareness of — растущее понимание чего-то.
be responsible for — быть причиной, отвечать за. Нужно прилагательное после is.
working conditions — условия труда; здесь множественное число: the poor conditions in which…
sustainable — экологичный, устойчивый; прилагательное перед collections.
Перед reduction нужно прилагательное: dramatic — резкое, значительное.
По смыслу «звучит старомодно»: old-fashioned или unfashionable. Просто fashionable противоречит смыслу (But… could be…).
the most effective thing — самое действенное. Ловушка: efficient — от другого корня и значит «экономный».

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.

q.first: 'I'll call you tomorrow,' Jack said to me.
q.expl: promise to do sth или promise (that) he would…. Tomorrow в косвенной речи → the next day.

q.expl: There's no point (in) doing sth — нет смысла что-то делать.

q.expl: be used to + -ing — привыкнуть к чему-то. Не путай с used to do — «раньше делал».

q.expl: Пассив в Present Perfect: hasn't been cleaned.

q.expl: so … that … couldn't ⇄ too + adj + to do: too tired to finish.

q.first: It's a pity I can't speak Italian.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a young memory champion. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Remember this
parts.subtitle: Eighteen-year-old Sofia Lind can memorise a shuffled pack of cards in under a minute. Daniel Price asked her how she does it.
paras: When I meet Sofia Lind in a busy café, the first thing she does is apologise for forgetting her purse. 'People always find that funny,' she says, 'but having a trained memory doesn't mean you remember everything. It means you remember the things you've decided to remember.' Last month, Sofia came third in an international memory competition, recalling the order of a shuffled pack of playing cards in just forty-one seconds.

Sofia insists that she was born with a perfectly ordinary memory. Her interest began at fourteen, when she borrowed a book about memory techniques from the library in the hope of improving her exam results. 'Most of it seemed ridiculous at first,' she admits. 'You're supposed to imagine strange, colourful scenes and put them in places you know well. But I tried it with a list of historical dates, and the next morning I could still remember all of them.'

The technique she uses for cards is based on the same idea. Each card is linked to a person, and each person to an action. 'The seven of hearts is my grandmother, for example, and she's always baking,' she explains. Memorising a pack means walking through her childhood home in her imagination, placing these characters in each room. 'It sounds complicated, but after a while it's as automatic as reading. You don't think about how to read a word, do you?'

Training takes up around an hour a day, which Sofia fits around her studies. She is honest about the downside. 'Some of my friends think it's a strange way to spend your time, and maybe they're right. There have definitely been evenings when I'd rather have been out with them.' But she has also noticed unexpected benefits. 'My concentration has improved enormously. I can sit in a noisy room and read without being distracted, which I never could before.'

So can anyone do what she does? Sofia thinks so, with one condition. 'You have to be willing to feel silly,' she says. 'The images that work best are the ones that are ridiculous or embarrassing. If you're too serious, your brain won't bother remembering them.' As we leave the café, she asks me to read out my phone number once – and then repeats it back to me, backwards.

q.stem: What point does Sofia make about her memory in the first paragraph?
opts: It works better for some kinds of information than others.
It only works well when she is relaxed.
It depends on a conscious decision to remember.
It has become less reliable since the competition.
q.hl: It means you remember the things you've decided to remember.
q.expl: Тренированная память — это помнить то, что ты решил запомнить. Поэтому кошелёк она забыла.

q.stem: Why did Sofia first read about memory techniques?
opts: She wanted to take part in competitions.
She hoped to do better at school.
A teacher recommended a book to her.
She was worried about her poor memory.
q.hl: in the hope of improving her exam results
q.expl: Она взяла книгу, надеясь улучшить оценки на экзаменах. Ловушка D: память у неё была обычная, а не плохая.

q.stem: How did Sofia feel about the techniques when she first read about them?
opts: She doubted that they would work.
She found them too complicated to try.
She thought they were only useful for history.
q.hl: Most of it seemed ridiculous at first
q.expl: Сначала всё казалось нелепым, то есть она сомневалась. Потом попробовала на датах, и сработало.

q.stem: What does Sofia compare memorising cards to?
opts: an everyday skill that no longer needs thought
q.hl: after a while it's as automatic as reading
q.expl: Со временем это так же автоматично, как чтение. Ловушка B: она «гуляет» по дому детства, но это знакомое место, а не новое. Ловушка D: бабушка — образ для карты, а не сравнение.

q.stem: What unexpected benefit has Sofia noticed from her training?
opts: Her friends have become more interested in memory.
She needs less time to study.
She is able to focus better.
She has become more confident with people.
q.expl: Концентрация сильно улучшилась: она может читать в шумной комнате.

q.stem: According to Sofia, what is necessary to develop a good memory?
q.hl: You have to be willing to feel silly
q.expl: Надо быть готовым чувствовать себя глупо: лучше всего работают нелепые образы. Серьёзность (B), наоборот, мешает, а о таланте (A) она говорит, что память у неё была обычная.

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a woman who started swimming in cold water. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Into the cold
parts.subtitle: Journalist Grace Walker was terrified of cold water. Then a friend persuaded her to try winter swimming.
paras: I have always hated being cold. So when my friend Maya suggested I join her for a swim in the lake near our town one January morning, I laughed. [[37]] Somehow, a week later, I found myself standing on the shore in a borrowed swimsuit, wondering what on earth I was doing.

The first few seconds were the worst physical experience of my life. My breath disappeared and every part of my body was screaming at me to get out. [[38]] After about a minute, however, something strange happened: the pain faded, and I felt calm and completely awake.

I stayed in for three minutes that day, which Maya assured me was plenty for a beginner. Getting dressed afterwards was almost as hard as the swim itself, because my fingers refused to work properly. [[39]] On the way home, though, I couldn't stop smiling.
Since then, I've swum at least once a week, and I've learned a lot about doing it safely. [[40]] Never swim alone, always have warm clothes ready, and get out long before you think you need to.

What I hadn't expected was the community. Every Saturday, a group of about twenty of us meets at the lake, and afterwards we share flasks of hot chocolate on the beach. [[41]] Our oldest member is seventy-eight; our youngest is a student of nineteen.
Scientists are still debating whether cold-water swimming has real health benefits. [[42]] What I do know is that I sleep better, feel happier and, strangely, no longer mind being cold.

sents.A: She didn't laugh back; she simply kept asking.
sents.B: Maya had warned me about this and told me to concentrate on breathing slowly.
sents.C: It took me ten minutes just to do up my coat.
sents.D: The rules are simple, but they matter.
sents.E: They are people I would never otherwise have met.
sents.F: I'm in no position to say who's right.
sents.G: Some days, the water is so cold that ice forms at the edges.

q.expl: Она рассмеялась, а Майя «не смеялась в ответ — просто продолжала звать» (A). Поэтому «somehow, a week later» она всё-таки на берегу.
Тело кричит «вылезай» → Майя предупреждала об этом и сказала дышать медленно (B) → «After about a minute… the pain faded».
Пальцы не слушались → десять минут застёгивала пальто (C) → «though, I couldn't stop smiling» — контраст.
«The rules are simple, but they matter» (D), а дальше сами правила: не плавать одному, тёплая одежда, выходить раньше.
Сообщество из двадцати человек → «people I would never otherwise have met» (E) → пример разнообразия: 78 лет и 19 лет.
Учёные спорят → «I'm in no position to say who's right» (F) → «What I do know is…». Ловушка G: про лёд можно было бы сказать где угодно, но ни один пропуск её не продолжает.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four students describe studying abroad. For questions 43–52, choose from the students (A–D). The students may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: A year abroad

texts.name: Lucas
texts.body: I knew Edinburgh would be colder than Madrid, but nothing prepared me for the wind. More difficult than the weather, though, was making friends. I'm quite shy, and for the first two months I spent most evenings alone in my room. Things changed when I joined the university hiking club on a whim. Spending whole days walking with the same people, you get to know them quickly. The only time I really struggled after that was the first Christmas, when I couldn't afford to fly home – I've never felt so far away from my family.

texts.name: Anna
texts.body: I'd studied Japanese for three years before I arrived in Osaka, so I assumed I'd cope. In reality, people spoke so fast that I understood almost nothing for the first few weeks. My host family were incredibly patient, and my host mother taught me to cook, which became our way of communicating when words failed. I made plenty of mistakes – I once addressed my professor far too casually, and I still go red thinking about it. But making mistakes is how you learn the unwritten rules.

texts.name: Kemal
texts.body: The biggest shock in Toronto was the cost of everything. Rent took more than half my monthly budget, so I found a part-time job in a bookshop within the first fortnight. Working twenty hours a week while studying was exhausting, but it taught me to plan every hour of my day. It also meant I had colleagues outside the university, which was a nice change. I came home a completely different person – much more independent, and much better with money.

texts.name: Julia
texts.body: In Brazil, my teachers always told us exactly what to read. In Berlin, the professor gave us a list of thirty books and said, 'Choose what interests you.' I panicked at first – I had no idea where to start. It took me a whole semester to get used to working that way, but now I can't imagine going back. I've applied for a master's programme here, and if I get a place, I'm planning to stay for at least another two years.

q.stem: felt isolated at the beginning of their stay?
q.hl: for the first two months I spent most evenings alone in my room
q.expl: Лукас первые два месяца проводил вечера один в комнате.
Анна думала, что справится с японским, а первые недели почти ничего не понимала.

q.stem: had to earn money to cover their living costs?
q.hl: I found a part-time job in a bookshop
q.expl: Аренда съедала больше половины бюджета, и Кемаль устроился в книжный магазин. Ловушка A: Лукасу не хватило денег на билет, но работу он не искал.

q.stem: struggled with a different approach to studying?
q.hl: I panicked at first – I had no idea where to start
q.expl: Джулия привыкла, что ей говорят, что читать, а в Берлине пришлось выбирать самой.

q.stem: made friends as a result of a spontaneous decision?
q.hl: I joined the university hiking club on a whim
q.expl: On a whim — по прихоти, спонтанно. В клубе походов Лукас и нашёл друзей.

q.stem: found a way of communicating that did not depend on language?
q.hl: which became our way of communicating when words failed
q.expl: Готовка с хозяйкой стала их способом общаться, когда не хватало слов.

q.stem: is still embarrassed by something they did?
q.hl: I still go red thinking about it
q.expl: Анна до сих пор краснеет, вспоминая, как слишком фамильярно обратилась к профессору.

q.stem: learned to organise their time more effectively?
q.hl: it taught me to plan every hour of my day
q.expl: Работа и учёба научили Кемаля планировать каждый час.

q.stem: hopes to extend their time abroad?
q.hl: I'm planning to stay for at least another two years
q.expl: Джулия подала документы в магистратуру и хочет остаться ещё минимум на два года.

q.stem: was unable to visit their family because of the cost?
q.hl: I couldn't afford to fly home
q.expl: На первое Рождество Лукасу не хватило денег на билет домой.
